analysis: **Where the pipeline improves.** On D1 and D2, the pipeline matched or exceeded Baseline A on all six model and dataset combinations, using smaller models available on a free tier rather than a frontier model. On D1, which removes identifying error names and adds red herrings, Qwen3.8 27B reached 100% with the pipeline against 92.5% from raw logs. Deterministic preprocessing cut input tokens by about half at the same LLM call count, and all 236 pipeline answers were usable, against 231 of 236 for Baseline A. Because each comparison uses at most 40 paired logs, we report these as directional results with exact p-values in Table 2, and larger sweeps are planned in Section 6.

**Where it performs similarly.** On D2, Qwen3.8 27B and gpt-oss-120b were 100% accurate in both LLM conditions across all 40 pairs, matching the 100% the proposal reported with Claude Opus on its own logs. Opus was not run on D2, so this is not a direct comparison. gpt-oss-20b reached 100% with the pipeline and 95% with Baseline A, from one false alarm and one empty answer on `no_fault` logs. On D1, gpt-oss-120b raised the same number of false alarms in both conditions (2 of 9 `no_fault` logs), so the summary did not protect it from red-herring errors. Confidence calibration was mixed: Brier score improved for Qwen3.8 27B (0.065 to 0.002), was flat for gpt-oss-120b (0.050 to 0.048), and worsened for gpt-oss-20b (0.028 to 0.048).

**Where it underperforms.** Baseline B, the rules-only control, scored 100% on both datasets, above every LLM condition. These datasets therefore saturate, so accuracy alone cannot show the value of the proposed system, which motivates the harder conditions in Section 6. On D1, gpt-oss-20b with the pipeline raised 2 false alarms where Baseline A raised none, although Baseline A returned empty answers on 2 other `no_fault` logs.

**Stakeholder logs (D3).** On the stakeholder's own 16 logs, for which the proposal published 16 of 16 with Claude Opus in both conditions, accuracy rose with model capability: gpt-oss-20b reached 13 of 16, gpt-oss-120b 15 of 16, and Qwen3.8 27B 16 of 16, matching the published Opus result on the same logs. All misses were `no_fault` logs labeled `slow_query`. The pipeline tied Baseline A on accuracy for every model while using 835 to 837 input tokens against 1,526 to 1,757. The rules control also scored 16 of 16. Our rebuilt parser reproduced the published summary for `pool_exhausted_run1` exactly, which supports the fidelity of the rebuild.

**Possible explanations.** We expected weaker models to benefit most from structure, and this pilot does not support that: the largest gain was on Qwen3.8 27B, which scores highest of the three on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. Its Baseline A misses on D1 included 2 `dependency_down` logs read as `pool_exhausted`, which the spacing fields directly address. That is suggestive only, because those fields were designed with the fault patterns in mind.

**Limits of this pilot.** A free-tier daily quota stopped gpt-oss-120b at 36 of 40 pairs on D1. D2 is complete at 40 pairs per model. D3 is complete at 16 pairs per model. The evidence rules were frozen after refinement on D1. On an earlier partial D2 run they flagged two runs, and manual inspection found both flags were scorer errors (for example, treating "3.2 ms above the baseline" as a latency measurement), and the flags on the full D2 run were not individually reviewed, so the Proposal criterion and Grounded columns may understate D2 and their ability to catch real fabrication remains unmeasured. **Not yet completed:** longer-log sweeps, a parser without spacing fields, a live Claude run, a recovery sweep, and any public benchmark.
